market_context: United States; FDA/FoodSafety.gov one-week refrigerated storage guidance
title: How long do hard-boiled eggs last in the fridge?

seo.title: How long do hard-boiled eggs last in the fridge?
seo.meta_description: Hard-boiled eggs keep for up to 1 week in the refrigerator at 40°F or below. Refrigerate within 2 hours and store peeled eggs covered.
seo.search_intent: Find the safe refrigerator storage time for hard-boiled eggs, peeled or unpeeled, and learn how to store them.

excerpt: Hard-boiled eggs can be refrigerated for up to 1 week, whether peeled or still in the shell, according to FDA guidance. Keep the refrigerator at 40°F (4°C) or below and refrigerate the eggs within 2 hours of cooking. The shell usually protects texture and moisture better; peeled eggs should be kept in a clean covered container.
content_html:
Hard-boiling an egg does not turn it into a shelf-stable food. Once cooked, it still needs refrigeration. FDA guidance gives hard-cooked eggs a refrigerator life of up to one week, peeled or unpeeled.

The simple rule: one week at 40°F or below

That one-week window assumes the eggs were cooked properly, chilled promptly, and kept in a refrigerator at 40°F (4°C) or colder.

If you batch-cook eggs, date the container. Smell and appearance cannot reconstruct how long an egg has been stored.

The shell helps protect quality

A cooked shell slows moisture loss and reduces direct exposure to refrigerator odors and handling. If you do not need the eggs peeled ahead of time, leaving the shell on usually keeps the texture better.

The shell does not make the egg shelf-stable. Cooked eggs still need refrigeration.

Store peeled eggs covered

Once peeled, the egg is directly exposed to air and hands. Keep peeled eggs in a clean covered container instead of leaving them uncovered on a refrigerator shelf.

They may dry out sooner than shell-on eggs even though the same one-week safety guideline applies.

Cool them promptly after cooking

Cold running water or an ice bath can stop carryover cooking and bring the temperature down quickly. After cooling, dry the eggs and refrigerate them rather than leaving the bowl on the counter for hours.

FDA's two-hour rule applies to refrigerated perishables: get them into the refrigerator within two hours, or within one hour if the surrounding temperature is above 90°F (32°C).

A sulfur smell does not always mean spoilage

Overcooked eggs can smell sulfurous, and a green-gray ring can form around the yolk from a reaction between iron and sulfur. Neither effect by itself means the egg is spoiled.

A truly rotten odor, slime, mold, or other obvious deterioration is a reason to discard it. But a normal smell should not be used to extend storage beyond the recommended time.

What about lunch boxes and picnics?

Hard-boiled eggs should stay cold if they will not be eaten within two hours. Use an insulated lunch bag or cooler with ice packs.

On a hot day above 90°F, the room-temperature limit drops to one hour.

Can you freeze hard-boiled eggs?

Whole hard-boiled eggs do not freeze well. The whites become rubbery and watery after thawing. It is usually better to cook only what you expect to eat within the week.

The rule worth remembering

One week in the refrigerator, chilled within two hours, and stored covered. The shell helps quality; refrigeration is what controls bacterial growth.

If the eggs sat out for hours or you cannot remember when they were cooked, the time-and-temperature history matters more than whether they still look normal.

faq.question: How long do unpeeled hard-boiled eggs last?
faq.answer: Up to 1 week in the refrigerator at 40°F or below.

faq.question: How long do peeled hard-boiled eggs last?
faq.answer: FDA gives the same one-week refrigerated window, but peeled eggs should be stored covered and may dry out sooner.

faq.question: Can I eat a hard-boiled egg left out overnight?
faq.answer: No. Refrigerated perishables should not sit at room temperature for more than 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F.
